a.event WHEN bitand(a.time_model, power(2, 18)) > 0 THEN 'CPU: IM Query' WHEN bitand(a.time_model, power(2, 19)) > 0 THEN 'CPU: IM Populate' WHEN bitand(a.time_model, power(2, 20)) > 0 THEN 'CPU: IM Prepopulate' WHEN bitand(a.time_model, power(2, 21)) > 0 THEN 'CPU: IM Repopulate' WHEN bitand(a.time_model, power(2, 22)) > 0 THEN 'CPU: IM Trickle Repop' ELSE 'CPU + Wait for CPU' END) as event, machine || ', ' || port as machine_port, nvl(module, 'NULL') as module, (CASE WHEN a.session_state = 'WAITING' AND a.event = 'enq: TM - contention' THEN GREATEST(NVL(a.p2, 0), 0) WHEN a.session_state Finding 2: Hard Parse Due to Literal Usage
Impact is 2.62 active sessions, 17% of total activity.
------------------------------------------------------
SQL statements were not shared due to the usage of literals. This resulted in
additional hard parses which were consuming significant database time.

   Recommendation 1: Application Analysis
   Estimated benefit is 2.62 active sessions, 17% of total activity.
   -----------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate application logic for possible use of bind variables instead
      of literals.
   Action
      Alternatively, you may set the parameter "cursor_sharing" to "force".
   Rationale

      11858394147190661821 and PLAN_HASH_VALUE 2893657747 were found to be

Finding 4: Commits and Rollbacks
Impact is 1.39 active sessions, 9.03% of total activity.
--------------------------------------------------------
Waits on event "log file sync" while performing COMMIT and ROLLBACK operations
were consuming significant database time.

   Recommendation 1: Application Analysis
   Estimated benefit is 1.39 active sessions, 9.03% of total activity.
   -------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate application logic for possible reduction in the number of
      COMMIT operations by increasing the size of transactions.
   Rationale
      The application was performing 53776 transactions per minute with an
      average redo size of 6208 bytes per transaction.

   Recommendation 2: Host Configuration
   Estimated benefit is 1.39 active sessions, 9.03% of total activity.
   -------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate the possibility of improving the performance of I/O to the
      online redo log files.
   Rationale
      The average size of writes to the online redo log files was 19 K and the
      average time per write was 1 milliseconds.
   Rationale
      The total I/O throughput on redo log files was 6.4 M per second for
      reads and 11 M per second for writes.
   Rationale
      The redo log I/O throughput was divided as follows: 0% by RMAN and
      recovery, 63% by Log Writer, 0% by Archiver, 0% by Streams AQ and 36% by
      all other activity.

   Symptoms That Led to the Finding:
   ---------------------------------
      Wait class "Commit" was consuming significant database time.
      Impact is 1.39 active sessions, 9.03% of total activity.

Finding 6: Shared Pool Latches
Impact is .61 active sessions, 3.96% of total activity.
-------------------------------------------------------
Contention for latches related to the shared pool was consuming significant
database time.
Waits for "library cache: mutex X" amounted to 1% of database time.
Waits for "latch: shared pool" amounted to 2% of database time.

   Recommendation 1: Application Analysis
   Estimated benefit is .61 active sessions, 3.96% of total activity.
   ------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate the cause for latch contention using the given blocking
      sessions or modules.
   Rationale
      The session with ID 3646 and serial number 3984 in instance number 1 was
      the blocking session responsible for 11% of this recommendation's
      benefit.
   Rationale
      The session was active in container PWS1E with database ID 1131385475.

   Symptoms That Led to the Finding:
   ---------------------------------
      Wait class "Concurrency" was consuming significant database time.
      Impact is 1.23 active sessions, 7.98% of total activity.


Finding 7: Hard Parse Due to Sharing Criteria
Impact is .43 active sessions, 2.82% of total activity.
-------------------------------------------------------
SQL statements with the same text were not shared because of cursor
environment mismatch. This resulted in additional hard parses which were
consuming significant database time.
Common causes of environment mismatch are session NLS settings, SQL trace
settings and optimizer parameters.

   Recommendation 1: Application Analysis
   Estimated benefit is .43 active sessions, 2.82% of total activity.
   ------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Look for top reason for cursor environment mismatch in
      V$SQL_SHARED_CURSOR.

   Symptoms That Led to the Finding:
   ---------------------------------
      Hard parsing of SQL statements was consuming significant database time.
      Impact is 3.05 active sessions, 19.82% of total activity.


Finding 8: Soft Parse
Impact is .34 active sessions, 2.22% of total activity.
-------------------------------------------------------
Soft parsing of SQL statements was consuming significant database time.

   Recommendation 1: Application Analysis
   Estimated benefit is .34 active sessions, 2.22% of total activity.
   ------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate application logic to keep open the frequently used cursors.
      Note that cursors are closed by both cursor close calls and session
      disconnects.

   Recommendation 2: Database Configuration
   Estimated benefit is .34 active sessions, 2.22% of total activity.
   ------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Consider increasing the session cursor cache size by increasing the
      value of parameter "session_cached_cursors".
   Rationale
      The value of parameter "session_cached_cursors" was "500" during the
      analysis period.
